topics.label: Course conclusion and lecture introduction
topics.groupedBecause: It provides the introductory framing for the lecture by outlining its learning objectives on cancer therapies.

topics.label: Conventional cancer therapies, systemic toxicity, and resistance
topics.groupedBecause: They discuss conventional modalities of cancer treatment—including surgery, radiotherapy, and cytotoxic chemotherapy—alongside their toxicities and common mechanisms of drug resistance.

topics.label: Exploiting intrinsic vulnerabilities and DNA repair defects
topics.groupedBecause: They cover therapeutic strategies designed to exploit specific biological vulnerabilities in cancer cells, including hormone dependence, cell cycle checkpoint deficiencies, and DNA repair defects.

topics.label: Targeted kinase inhibitors, oncogene addiction, and resistance mechanisms
topics.groupedBecause: They examine targeted therapies directed against driver oncogenic kinases and the mechanisms of resistance and drug addiction that arise during treatment.

topics.label: Antibody-based cancer therapies
topics.groupedBecause: They detail the therapeutic use of engineered antibodies to target cancer cells directly or deliver cytotoxic payloads as antibody-drug conjugates.

topics.label: Immune surveillance and T-cell-directed immunotherapies
topics.groupedBecause: They explore the evidence for immune surveillance against tumors and the application of immunotherapies that harness and engineer T cells to eliminate cancer cells.

topics.label: Global progress, challenges, and future paradigms in cancer treatment
topics.groupedBecause: They reflect on historical progress, ongoing therapeutic challenges, ethical considerations, and future paradigms in cancer research and clinical management.
